extracted.intended_audience: student and trainee journalists; practising journalists adapting to print, broadcast, and digital formats
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for selecting, structuring, and writing news and feature journalism across print, broadcast, and digital formats (UK-oriented). Emphasises newsworthiness, lead construction, style, verification, and adaptations for online/shortform and longform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topicality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should be timely; current events and recent developments carry priority in news selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose stories that affect many people or have important consequences; emphasise scale and consequences to demonstrate importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events nearer to the audience are more newsworthy; local angle increases reader interest and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions or statements by well-known individuals or institutions raise newsworthiness; attach notable names where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories involving disagreement, struggle or confrontation are inherently newsworthy; highlight opposing forces and tensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items that generate sympathy, surprise or emotional engagement with readers; use human detail to connect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unexpected or bizarre occurrences attract attention; emphasise the unusualness or the 'oddness' of the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex / scandal (tabloid context)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensational sexual or scandalous elements increase tabloid appeal; use cautiously and ethically, respecting privacy and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories with economic impact, financial stakes or monetary consequences are newsworthy; highlight costs, losses, gains or market effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Most important fact first; Active voice; 25 words or fewer (often); Captures essence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the central news nugget up front (inverted-pyramid lead for hard news); prefer active constructions, concision (often ~25 words or fewer) and a sentence that encapsulates the story's essence and hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Inverted pyramid (hard news); Narrative structure (features); Q&A (interviews); Listicle (some online)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match story-shape to format and audience: use inverted pyramid for urgent/hard news, narrative and character-driven arcs for features/longform, Q&A for interview pieces, and list formats when suited to short online consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing style
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear, simple language; Short sentences; Avoid jargon; Active voice; Concrete > abstract; Specific > general; Show > tell
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise clarity and readability: use short sentences, common vocabulary, concrete detail and specificity. Prefer active voice and examples that show rather than abstract statements. Avoid unexplained technical terms and unnecessary complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple sources; Named where possible; Document trails; Quotes accurate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify facts with more than one source, name sources when appropriate, keep documentation or paper trails to support claims, and ensure quoted material is reproduced accurately. Verification must be practicable within newsroom deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortform online adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: Shortform: more news values applied per word
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing short online pieces, compress news values and select the most potent facts per word; make every sentence carry newsworthiness and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longform online adaptation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longform digital journalism needs narrative development, characterisation and depth; invest in scene-setting, arc and rich detail rather than just facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headlines (online)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft headlines that balance clarity, keyword/search suitability and social appeal; aim for concise, compelling phrasing that works for search engines and social platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile-first considerations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design copy and structure for mobile consumption: short paragraphs, scannable leads, clear headings, and content that hooks quickly on small screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story-shape fit (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Story-shape — fits available format (200 words, 800 words, 2000 words)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a story's material fits the intended length/format; trim or expand reporting to match target word-count and platform expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline-able
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the story yields a tight, attention-grabbing headline (often 8–10 words) that summarises the hook and entices clicks or reads.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-paragraph compelling
rubrics_metrics.description: First-paragraph compelling — hooks reader in first line
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the opening line or first paragraph immediately engages the reader and sets up the primary question or conflict that the story resolves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote-worthy sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify sources who provide memorable, quotable lines that convey authority, emotion or colour; such quotes enhance readability and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual potential
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer stories that lend themselves to strong photos, video or graphics; visual assets increase engagement across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader-resonant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose angles and details that connect with the target audience's experiences, concerns or interests to maximise relevance and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiable within deadline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether essential facts, sources and documentation can be checked within the available time; if not, the piece may need reframing or delay.
